turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".
turns.answer_text:
From the data, the highest fatigue strengths come from a distinct upper-end process/composition region rather than from the middle of the full design space. The strongest samples (>1000 MPa) share these features:

- Process route near the high-strength branch: high NT/CT, active Ct/DT/Dt, low THT/THt/THQCr, TT in the 160–200 range, Tt near 120, and TCr near 0.5.
- Composition: low-to-moderate C (~0.17–0.23), moderate Si (~0.20–0.35), Mn ~0.5–0.85, low P/S, and meaningful Ni–Cr–Mo alloying.
- Robustness evidence: nearby high-target samples vary Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, Ni/Cr balance, and RedRatio by amounts much larger than ±5% while still remaining in the upper plateau. This suggests a broad high-strength region rather than a single sharp spike.

The absolute best observed row is at several boundary values. To keep the recipe robust under a ±5% single-variable perturbation, I pull boundary-dominated variables slightly inward so that the perturbed values remain feasible, while keeping the recipe centered in the high-target plateau. For variables with clear plateau behavior (Ct, DT, Dt, QmT, TT, composition), I choose central plateau values rather than the most extreme observed point.
